items.text: Your college rulebook decides what happens next, not a general rule.
There is no single national rule for carrying backlogs into second year.
Choose stay, switch or leave by a date.

blocks.heading: Routes Are Ordered By How Far

items.text: The routes are ordered by how far visible skill can lift income.
Employers in these fields look at projects and the way you explain them.
Who pays you Startups, small firms and clients who buy a finished project; later, product companies.

blocks.heading: Check the Fit
rows: You carry a few failed subjects into second year and clear them in later exams, within the limit your college allows.
Register for the backlog exams at the first chance and plan the clearing order.
You do not meet the promotion rule and repeat the year or the failed courses.
Ask the exam cell exactly what you must repeat and by when.
Failed because of attendance or internal marks
The detention is course-wise, and the end-semester exam may not be open to you.
Ask what remedial or re-registration option exists for each course.
Passed, but the marks are low
No failure, but the branch or the college does not suit you.
Treat this as a fit problem, not a pass-or-fail problem, and use the routes below.

blocks.heading: How Promotion Rules Differ Between Colleges
rows: TCET, Mumbai (examination cell page, year not stated)

For BE, B.Tech and B.Voc, a student may move into the second year by passing every course in Semesters I and II, or by failing no more than eight subjects in the two semesters, with no more than five of those failures from end-semester exams.
Some colleges allow a fairly large number of backlogs. The page does not say what happens above the limit, so ask.

To move up, a student must earn 50 percent of the previous year's credits. Those who do not "will consequently lose one academic year". Failed courses are repeated, and a student may take up to twelve semesters to finish an eight-semester programme.
Credit-based rules turn a failed first year into a repeat year. A longer maximum duration gives more time, but it costs fees.

figures.label: Remaining Education Budget
figures.source: Our strongest suggestion: keep a degree fee near a tenth of the family's total education budget, and treat spending above roughly a fifth as a serious caution. An illustration, not a real fee: on a Rs 12 lakh education budget, a tenth is Rs 1.2 lakh, and the rest can fund backlog fees, a laptop, one skill course, a project and a reserve for an extra year.

blocks.heading: Clearing Backlogs Without Losing the Next Year

items.text: Sort failed courses by difficulty and by how many marks you were short.
Clear the course with the nearest exam first; confidence helps with the harder ones.
Avoid registering for too many backlog courses along with the current semester.
Use the remedial term where the college offers one; MITAOE's rules describe a short remedial term for declared courses.
NPTEL courses from the IITs and IISc, which are free to learn, with an optional paid exam only if you need the certificate.
YouTube lessons and official documentation for a language or tool such as Python, spreadsheets or CAD.
Open courseware and good textbooks, to repair the first-year subjects you failed.
A project built with classmates, and college clubs, labs and internships where you can show your work.
